item.title: Kinoya father says spending time with his children helps him unwind
item.description: As we celebrate Father’s Day today, Kinoya father Rupeni Veremadigi says there is no greater joy than seeing his children happy. A father of four, Veremadigi says the smiles of his children make the challenges of a busy day worthwhile.
item.content:encoded:
As we celebrate Father’s Day today, Kinoya father Rupeni Veremadigi says there is no greater joy than seeing his children happy.

A father of four, Veremadigi says the smiles of his children make the challenges of a busy day worthwhile.

He recently brought his children to the Hibiscus Baby Show at the Suva Civic Centre, giving him another opportunity to spend quality time with his family.

Veremadigi says while work can be tiring, spending time with his children helps him unwind and reminds him of the blessings of being a father.

Insert: Veremadigi – Kids are eagerly waiting for you Sept 02

The family’s day at the Baby Show on Wednesday ended on an even happier note, with one of his children winning a prize sponsored by Drypers.

For Veremadigi, moments like these are a reminder that despite the demands of fatherhood, seeing his children happy makes it all worthwhile.

item.title: Digital system to strengthen maternal and child healthcare in Fiji
item.description: Healthcare workers in Fiji will soon have a better way to track high-risk pregnancies and follow up with vulnerable mothers and children. This comes as the PATISPlus patient information system is introduced to maternal and child health clinics in Fiji for the first time.
item.content:encoded:
Healthcare workers in Fiji will soon have a better way to track high-risk pregnancies and follow up with vulnerable mothers and children.

This comes as the PATISPlus patient information system is introduced to maternal and child health clinics in Fiji for the first time.

The Ministry of Health and Medical Services, in partnership with the JICA ResPACT Project, recently trained 18 nurses in Suva to use the digital system.

PATISPlus will connect patient information across different stages of care, from pregnancy and delivery through to postnatal care.

The system will help healthcare workers track high-risk pregnancies, share important patient information and follow up with vulnerable patients.

It will also support health services during natural disasters and disease outbreaks by helping clinics identify and prioritise patients when resources are limited.

Following the initial training, the programme will be expanded to pilot sites across the Northern, Western and Eastern Divisions.

The initiative is part of ongoing efforts to use digital technology to strengthen healthcare delivery and create a more connected and resilient health system for mothers and children across Fiji.

item.title: RBF issues warning over unauthorised foreign exchange activities
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Fiji is warning members of the public to only conduct foreign exchange transactions with licensed dealers, as dealing with unauthorised operators could expose them to fraud, loss of money and a lack of legal protection. This comes after the Reserve Bank of Fiji received information that some businesses, hotels and individuals are engaging in foreign exchange activities without
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank of Fiji is warning members of the public to only conduct foreign exchange transactions with licensed dealers, as dealing with unauthorised operators could expose them to fraud, loss of money and a lack of legal protection.

This comes after the Reserve Bank of Fiji received information that some businesses, hotels and individuals are engaging in foreign exchange activities without the required licence.

It says that while hotels and retail businesses are allowed to accept foreign currency from tourists as payment for goods or services, they cannot provide money-changing services to other customers unless they are licensed to do so.

The RBF stresses that any change given to customers must be in Fijian dollars, while foreign currency received must be deposited with a commercial bank or sold to a licensed restricted foreign exchange dealer within 30 days.

It adds six commercial banks are currently authorised to conduct foreign exchange business in Fiji including ANZ Bank, Bank of Baroda, BSP Financial Group (Fiji) Pte Limited, BRED Bank (Fiji) Limited, HFC Bank and Westpac Banking Corporation.

It says there are also eight licensed restricted foreign exchange dealers including City Forex (Fiji) Pty Limited, Singapore Exchange, FEXCO (Fiji) Limited, Lotus Foreign Exchange Limited, MH Money Express Limited Fiji, Real Forex Proprietary (Fiji) Limited, GCC Exchange Limited and Vision Fintech Services Pte Limited.

The RBF says enforcement action will be taken against unauthorised operators in accordance with the Exchange Control Act 1950.

People who suspect unlicensed foreign exchange activities or other unauthorised financial services are being encouraged to report them through the RBF’s Confidential Disclosures portal.

item.title: SJSS week-long platinum jubilee begins today
item.description: Saint Joseph’s Secondary School is set to celebrate a historic milestone this week as it marks 70 years of educating and empowering women through a week-long Platinum Jubilee celebration, beginning today. The celebrations will bring together past and present students, staff, and members of the wider school community for a programme filled with faith, culture, sisterhood, reflection and celebration
item.content:encoded:
Saint Joseph’s Secondary School is set to celebrate a historic milestone this week as it marks 70 years of educating and empowering women through a week-long Platinum Jubilee celebration, beginning today.

The celebrations will bring together past and present students, staff, and members of the wider school community for a programme filled with faith, culture, sisterhood, reflection and celebration.

The Platinum Jubilee officially begins tomorrow with an Opening Mass at 10am at Mt St Mary’s Church.

The celebrations continue on Monday, September 7, with a morning fitness session at Zenergy Gym, followed by a welcome cocktail at the SJSS Hall at 5pm.

On Tuesday, September 8, the programme will feature a Law and Governance Breakfast at 8.30am at the Fiji Museum Café, followed by a visit to State House at Government House at 11am.

The evening will continue at the SJSS Hall from 6pm, with organisers promising an unforgettable evening of culture, laughter, sisterhood and music.

Wednesday, September 9, will begin with a morning walk at 7am, starting from the Suva Bowling Club and ending at the Nasese Seafront .

A post-walk breakfast will follow at 8.30am, hosted by the SJSS Alumnae medics, with a timely discussion on body autonomy .

The evening will feature a Flower Power Tekiteki Night at Paradiso Restaurant from 5pm, followed by an Island Night at the Suva Bowling Club at 6.30pm.

On Thursday, September 10, alumnae and guests will have the opportunity to explore the city during a Bus Tour of Old Suva, departing from Albert Park at 10am.

A prefects’ school tour will be held at 1pm, before the day concludes with the Bold and Beautiful 90s Quiz and Disco at 5pm at the Fiji Museum Deck.

Friday, September 11, will be the Jubilee Celebration Day, beginning at 9am at the SJSS School Hall.

The day will continue with a Pure Fiji tour and shopping experience at 12.30pm, followed by the SJSS Alumnae March at 3pm at the SJSS Sports Field.

The Platinum Legacy Cocktail and Fashion Show will then take centre stage at 6pm at the Fiji Museum Deck.

Next Saturday, will celebrate the diversity and richness of the Pacific with Pacific Market Day from 9.30am at the SJSS School Hall.

The celebrations will reach one of their major highlights that evening with the Pacific Elegance Gala at 6pm at the Vodafone Arena.

The week-long milestone will conclude on Sunday, September 13, with a Closing Mass at 1pm at Sacred Heart Cathedral.

item.title: Paddle for Hope continues its journey around Viti Levu
item.description: Karishma Kumari , Temalesi Vono · 06/09/2026 The Paddle for Hope team continues its more than 500-kilometre journey around Viti Levu, taking a strong message to communities about protecting Fiji’s oceans and reducing reliance on single-use plastics.
item.content:encoded:
Karishma Kumari , Temalesi Vono · 06/09/2026

The Paddle for Hope team continues its more than 500-kilometre journey around Viti Levu, taking a strong message to communities about protecting Fiji’s oceans and reducing reliance on single-use plastics.

The team started its journey from the National Sailing Centre in Suva, travelling along the Suva Foreshore before continuing to Muaivuso.

On Day 2, the team visited Togoru and Navua, before heading to Rovadrau, the Pearl Resort and Lomary on Day 3.

The team then visited Galoa and Navutulevu, where they were welcomed by villagers and given an opportunity to share the message behind the campaign.

They explained how single-use plastics can enter the food chain and potentially affect people’s health and wellbeing, while also encouraging communities to take greater responsibility for keeping their surroundings and waterways clean.

The team also thanked the people of Navutulevu Village for their hospitality and for providing a platform to share the campaign’s message.

The journey is part of the SUP Against SUP initiative, which stands for Stand Up Paddling Against Single-Use Plastics, using the Paddle for Hope journey to promote cleaner oceans and healthier communities.

During the visit, the Ministry of Environment also delivered a presentation on recycling and waste management, highlighting the importance of responsible waste disposal and reducing waste at its source.

The Paddle for Hope team says the journey continues to bring the message directly to communities, encouraging people to make small but meaningful changes in their daily lives to help protect Fiji’s marine environment.

item.title: No one charged yet in alleged overseas employment scam involving more than 300 Fijians
item.description: Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026 Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.
item.content:encoded:
Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026

Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.

More than 300 people claim they paid $100 each after being promised overseas employment opportunities, with some expecting to travel to Australia.

They say over 50 people reportedly turned up at the Nadi International Airport last Saturday expecting to travel overseas but later discovered that there were no flight bookings for them.

Some of those affected had reportedly resigned from their jobs in preparation for the promised overseas employment.

The Ministry of Employment is urging those affected to lodge reports with Police and stresses that workers are not required to pay recruitment fees to participate in Government-facilitated overseas employment programmes.
